=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel — Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary point — the "Reviewer Efficiency Note."** The Seller's package asks us to treat every clause marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides" and to review only [OPEN] items (there are none). Nothing in the Seller's own documents has been agreed by Wattlebridge; a Seller cannot pre-clear its own positions. I have disregarded the labels and reviewed the whole package. The [STANDARD] tags actually sit on the most buyer-adverse terms, which is itself a signal.

Read as a whole, the Seller's Disclosure Letter is more candid than the Seller Update. The Letter repeatedly admits that key items are *not* done (Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge, Ironquay payment, bonus funding, incident investigation), while the Update characterises the same items as "addressed", "adequate" or "not material". The gap between the two is where our mark-up should concentrate.

---

## A. Liability package (cl. 12–13)

**1. Cap at 20% / AUD 4.8m applied to *all* claims.**
Reasonable as a general-warranty cap in isolation, but the Seller then stretches it to fundamental warranties, tax, IP and (via cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5) to indemnities and "all Claims of any nature". Push back:
- Title/capacity/authority warranties: 100% of price, no de minimis/basket, 6–7 year (or statutory limitation) survival. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason to cap title to shares at 20% of what we are paying for them.
- Tax warranties and tax indemnity: separate cap (at least 100% of price), survival to expiry of ATO amendment periods plus a margin (typically 7 years).
- Specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006, Bluefen): outside the cap, basket and de minimis entirely. Indemnities are dollar-for-dollar risk allocation for *known* issues; subjecting them to the basket defeats their purpose.
- Fraud/wilful concealment: carve out from every limitation.

**2. De minimis AUD 25,000 / basket AUD 250,000, deductible structure.**
Thresholds are within market range for a AUD 24m deal, but: (a) push for a tipping basket (recover from the first dollar once exceeded) rather than excess-only; (b) allow aggregation of related claims arising from the same facts so that, for example, the three Sandbar renewals or the 1,240 records in DD-006 cannot be sliced beneath the de minimis.

**3. 18-month notice period for general warranties.**
Acceptable for general warranties provided it covers one full audit cycle post-Completion (we should confirm the FY27 audit timing — 24 months is safer). Not acceptable for tax, title or indemnities, and the catch-all "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" should be reversed: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

**4. Cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 — exclusive remedy and non-reliance across "all Claims."**
Non-reliance language must not exclude reliance on the warranties, disclosure letter and specific indemnities themselves, and cannot exclude statutory remedies (misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL cannot be contracted out of in any event, but the drafting should not attempt it). Carve out fraud, the indemnities, the tax covenant and equitable/injunctive relief.

## B. Disclosure and knowledge (Sch. 7, cl. 8.3)

**5. General disclosure of the entire data room and "public registers".**
Reject the blanket approach. Buyer position: only matters *fairly disclosed* — with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter — qualify the warranties. General disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records" (undefined; effectively unlimited) should be deleted or limited to specified ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches as at a stated date. The Disclosure Letter's own §11 reservation ("the Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement") confirms the Seller is trying to shift the diligence burden onto us by volume.

**6. Cl. 8.3 Buyer knowledge — "any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."**
This is the single most dangerous drafting point. "Discoverable" (not "actually known") combined with the general disclosure would mean virtually nothing is claimable. Strike entirely, or at most limit to actual knowledge of named Wattlebridge individuals of a matter that constitutes a breach, excluding constructive knowledge and anything the Seller argues could have been found. Add a clause that the Buyer's investigations do not qualify or reduce any Warranty.

## C. The known issues — mismatch between Update and Disclosure Letter

**7. Bluefen (DD-002; ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue).**
Update says "addressed" and consent satisfied on "delivery of written consent". Disclosure Letter admits no written consent exists and no evidence the cl. 11.3 conditions have been met. Position:
- Condition precedent to Completion: unconditional written consent *in a form acceptable to the Buyer*, with the cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, delivered pre-Completion; "reasonable endeavours" becomes "best endeavours" with Buyer involvement in the approach to Bluefen.
- Warranty that there has been no notice of termination, re-pricing or reduction in scope from Bluefen.
- If the Seller resists a CP: price reduction/escrow sized to the revenue at risk, or a post-Completion indemnity for loss of the contract within 12 months.

**8. Riverlark facility (DD-003; ~AUD 3.2m).**
The headline deal is debt-free/cash-free; a "release to be provided following Completion" means we buy a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and an unmet change-of-control clause (cl. 8.1), with the lender able to call an event of default on day one. Position: repayment from Seller proceeds via the funds flow, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered *at* Completion as a deliverable; the AUD 3.2m plus break costs/interest to be deducted from the price under the debt-free mechanics. If timing genuinely requires post-Completion discharge, hold back the amount in escrow and take a specific indemnity.

**9. Closing bonuses (DD-005; AUD 420,000 plus on-costs).**
The Update says they are "a matter for the Seller" but they are not in the funds flow and the Company — which we will own — is the employer and payer. Position: treat as Transaction Expenses/debt-like item, deducted from the price including superannuation, payroll tax and PAYG withholding (budget ~AUD 480–500k gross-up), or paid by the Seller at Completion with a specific indemnity. Confirm whether the "continued-employment" condition creates a retention tail that falls post-Completion.

**10. Ironquay IP (DD-004 / DD-010; AUD 180,000 open).**
Title to SOW3 Project Materials does not pass until *every* SOW3 fee is cleared; AUD 180k is open and there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment. If those materials sit in the product, we are not buying the IP. Position: Completion deliverable of (a) bank evidence of payment and (b) executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay; IP warranty that the Company owns or validly licenses all IP used in the business; specific indemnity uncapped and outside the basket for any failure of title to Ironquay-developed IP, not limited to the AUD 180k payment. Confirm whether other SOWs have similar conditions.

**11. Export/privacy incident (DD-006; ~1,240 records).**
"Preliminary" and "not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation; the Letter admits scope, access and notifiability are unknown. Under the Privacy Act (as amended) an eligible data breach assessment must be completed within 30 days of suspicion — we need the date of the incident and the assessment status. Position: pre-signing completion of the assessment with Buyer access to the findings; specific indemnity (outside cap/basket) for notification costs, regulatory penalties, third-party claims and remediation; warranty of compliance with privacy law and no other incidents; a condition if the OAIC becomes involved pre-Completion. Also check whether the records are Bluefen's or another customer's data, which would trigger contractual notification obligations.

**12. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; 3 × AUD 110,000).**
The split into three AUD 110k contracts across two data-room documents is notable: individually each sits near the de minimis and well inside the basket. Ask the Seller to confirm whether these are committed, terminable, and whether they were in the FY26 forecast. If they are new or accelerated commitments, treat as leakage or a working-capital adjustment; at minimum, aggregate for claim purposes and ensure the locked-box/completion-accounts mechanism captures them.

**13. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).**
The Seller's characterisation ("only notification"; "no consent merely because shares are sold") is a legal conclusion, not a disclosure. Have our team read the clauses directly. If notification is required, make it a Completion deliverable. For Mossvale, confirm the assignment restriction has no change-of-control limb and whether the relationship is material.

**14. Tax / IP "settled under the general regime".**
Not acceptable — see item 1. We need a standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, including the bonus-related liabilities), a tax warranty survival period aligned with amendment periods, and IP warranties with a separate cap. Ask for GST/stamp-duty treatment confirmation (NSW landholder duty should be assessed given the office lease).

**15. Title verification (DD-012).**
A share register is maintained by the Company itself; it is evidence, not proof. Run an ASIC current and historical company extract and PPSR search against both Paperbark and Harbourglass (the Riverlark security may extend to the shares), and require delivery of share certificates, transfer forms, and board/shareholder resolutions at Completion. Title warranty remains fundamental and uncapped.

## D. Items the Seller did not raise

- **Material adverse change / interim covenants** between signing and Completion — ensure Bluefen, Riverlark and DD-006 developments are covered and that the Seller must notify us of any breach.
- **W&I insurance** — if the Seller wants a 20% cap, a buy-side policy may bridge the gap; but known issues (7–11 above) will be excluded, so the specific indemnities are essential regardless.
- **Escrow/retention** — with this many open items, a retention of 10–15% of price for 12–18 months is justified.
- **Restraints, key employees** — not mentioned; confirm non-compete from Harbourglass and retention arrangements for the DD-005 bonus recipients post-Completion.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Recommended position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Efficiency note" / [STANDARD] labels | Disregard; nothing is agreed. Note for the record that the Buyer has reviewed all clauses. |
| 2 | Cap / basket / time limits | 20% cap only for general warranties; 100% for title/capacity/tax; indemnities and fraud outside all limitations; tipping basket; aggregation of related claims; tax survival ~7 years. |
| 3 | Non-reliance / exclusive remedy | Carve out warranties, disclosure letter, indemnities, tax covenant, fraud and statutory rights. |
| 4 | General disclosure | Fair-disclosure standard only; delete "public records" or list specific searches. |
| 5 | Buyer knowledge (cl. 8.3) | Delete; at most actual knowledge of named individuals; Buyer diligence does not qualify warranties. |
| 6 | Bluefen | CP: unconditional written consent in Buyer-acceptable form before Completion; fallback escrow/indemnity. |
| 7 | Riverlark | Repay from proceeds at Completion; release and PPSR discharge as deliverables; deduct from price. |
| 8 | Bonuses | Treat as transaction expense with on-costs in funds flow / price reduction; Seller indemnity. |
| 9 | Ironquay | Payment evidence + confirmatory assignment at Completion; uncapped IP indemnity, not limited to AUD 180k. |
| 10 | DD-006 incident | Complete breach assessment pre-signing; uncapped specific indemnity; privacy warranties. |
| 11 | Sandbar renewals | Confirm status; aggregate; capture in price mechanics if not ordinary course. |
| 12 | Lease / Mossvale | Independent review of clauses; notifications as deliverables. |
| 13 | Tax / IP | Separate warranties, tax indemnity and caps. |
| 14 | Title | Independent ASIC/PPSR verification; full Completion deliverables; uncapped title warranty. |
| 15 | Structure | Retention/escrow of 10–15%; consider W&I for the general package. |

**Overall:** the Seller's Update presents a package in which the three largest known risks (a 30% customer, AUD 3.2m of secured debt and unresolved IP title) are either deferred past Completion or left to the Buyer, while the limitation and knowledge clauses would make them effectively unclaimable afterwards. Our mark-up should insist that known issues are fixed *before* we pay, and that the liability regime is reserved for the unknown.
